sections.content:
10,325 people

were counted on the census as "sheet metal workers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Sheet metal workers mark out, cut, shape and join sheet metal using hand or machine tools to make and repair sheet metal products and components (excluding vehicle bodywork).

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "sheet metal workers" there were more men than women (97.5% compared with 2.5%).

This means "sheet metal workers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 97.5% and women made up 2.5% of "sheet metal workers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sheet metal workers" included:

  • groundsmen and greenkeepers
  • vehicle paint technicians
  • tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "sheet metal workers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "sheet metal workers", 15.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sheet metal workers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sheet metal workers" included:

  • gardeners and landscape gardeners
  • footwear and leather working trades
  • library clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sheet metal workers", 8.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92.4% compared with 7.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.1%) than self-employed (9.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Kirklees, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
